topic: The Additive Property of Normal Distributions: Gaussian + Gaussian = Gaussian

sections.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (1 min)
sections.content: Briefly recall the bell curve (Normal Distribution) defined by Mean (μ) and Variance (σ²). Introduce the concept of independent random variables.
sections.example: Visual: Two separate, static bell curves on a screen. One labeled 'Morning Coffee Prep Time', one labeled 'Commute Time'.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Convolution (1.5 mins)
sections.content: Explain that adding two independent random variables is mathematically a 'convolution' of their probability density functions (PDFs). Visually demonstrate how the density spreads out.
sections.example: Animation: The two bell curves merge into one. The resulting curve is wider (higher variance) and centered at the sum of the means (μ1+μ2).

sections.title: The Mathematical Rule (1 min)
sections.content: Define the formal rule: If X ~ N(μ1, σ1²) and Y ~ N(μ2, σ2²), then (X+Y) ~ N(μ1+μ2, σ1²+σ2²). Highlight that the variances add, not the standard deviations.
sections.example: Visual: A scoreboard showing Mean: 5 + 3 = 8; Variance: 2 + 4 = 6. Resulting curve parameters displayed dynamically.

sections.title: Real-World Application (1.5 mins)
sections.content: Applying the concept to signal processing or logistics. Explain why error margins aggregate in complex systems.
sections.example: Animation: A robot delivery drone has a delivery window with a normal distribution. Adding the 'assembly time' and 'travel time' variances helps calculate the final probability of arriving before 5 PM.
